verdict.rationale: Jitsu documents a code-first workflow for its automations (Functions): you build them from your own repo with jitsu-cli, which scaffolds a TypeScript project with tests and deploys it to the workspace. jitsu-cli also manages workspace configuration objects, so automations can be kept in source control and reviewed there, and an audit log records account activity. However, versioning and review rely on the user's own repo, and rollback is only implied by redeploying an earlier version; Jitsu documents no native version history, diff, or rollback. Missing for 10: native version history for functions and pipeline config, an in-product review or approval flow, a documented one-step rollback, and independent hands-on corroboration.
